events.summary: Owner ruling on the design version identity contradiction: DEFER the re-title to the next cascade rather than pay it now. The pinned design (sha256 c4bb6f67..., 2072 lines) reads v1.24 on line 1 while section 23.22 at line 2027 is titled a v1.25 change log, and v1.25 occurs exactly once in the document. gpt-5.6-sol graded this BLOCKING across rounds 3 and 4; gemini-3.7-flash-high, given it as an explicit tie-break, agreed with Sol and wrote that the design must be re-titled, noting that leaning on the byte and line-count pin repeats the rejected protected-path rationale. claude-opus-5 graded it a NIT because the gate pins bytes and total_lines and never reads the version string. The owner was told that re-titling moves design_file_sha256, which the receipt pins, forcing a full cascade and a fresh Section-16 review, and was offered re-title now, defer, or overrule as a nit. He selected DEFER and typed no free text. This is a deferral, not a closure: the finding remains open and 2 of 3 reviewers hold it BLOCKING. It must be paid at the next amendment that moves the design.

CORRECTION of record, issued by the Lead against its own earlier statements. Two claims this session put into the permanent record are false and are withdrawn here rather than edited in place. (1) The Lead told the owner, and event HIST-2026-0021 records as the reason the design contradiction could be graded a NIT, that the gate pins bytes and total_lines and never reads the design version string. That is untrue. verify_bceg.py:503 extracts the version from line 1 with re.search(r"\bDesign (v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+)\s*$"), design_version is a member of SEMANTIC_COVERAGE_REVIEW_CONTENT_IDENTITY_KEYS at lines 66-74, and lines 650-654 refuse via _semantic_review_invalid when any such key differs from the receipt. design_version is therefore a machine-consumed, gate-enforced identity. claude-opus-5 found this in round 5 and reversed its own rounds-3 and -4 NIT grades on that basis; the Lead then verified it directly. The owner granted the HIST-2026-0021 deferral on this false premise. (2) WP_P012_R30_REPAIR5_PATCH_PLAN.md section 2 and commit 4eb75b44 both assert that the D026 predicate tests the contradiction rather than any wording and so cannot be satisfied by phrasing. That is untrue: both flagships measured that rewording the unrepaired text from "NONACCEPTED until forward repin F30" to a synonym flips the predicate GREEN with the contradiction intact, because the check is a single literal substring test. The repair itself is unaffected and was independently verified correct by both auditors; the claim about the predicate is what was wrong. Commit 4eb75b44 is immutable and is corrected here rather than rewritten.

events.summary: Owner ruling: OVERRULE the design version identity contradiction as a NIT, superseding the DEFER recorded in HIST-2026-0021. The ruling was taken after the Lead corrected its own false statement and told the owner that design_version IS read and enforced by the gate (verify_bceg.py:503, :66-74, :650-654), which is the opposite of what he was told when he granted the deferral. Measured position at the time of ruling: the pinned design reads v1.24 on line 1, section 23.22 at line 2027 is titled a v1.25 change log, v1.25 occurs exactly once in 2072 lines, and the receipt certifies design_version v1.24 - so the enforced identity matches today and the gate passes, while the receipt certifies a version older than the amendment it certifies. The owner was offered three routes: re-title and pay a full cascade plus a fresh Section-16 review, overrule as a NIT with the corrected facts, or stop and leave the package blocked. He selected the overrule and typed no free text. DISSENT RECORDED, and it is unanimous among the reviewers: gpt-5.6-sol graded this BLOCKING in rounds 3, 4 and 5 and wrote that the package is not acceptable while it remains; claude-opus-5 graded it BLOCKING in round 5 after reversing its own earlier NIT grades; gemini-3.7-flash-high, given it as an explicit tie-break, wrote that the design must be re-titled. No reviewer supports this ruling. It is an owner acceptance of a named risk over unanimous reviewer dissent, and it must not be read later as a technical clearance.
